g.text: Original educational diagrams • static reference • conceptual examples
Dedicated link between two endpoints; not peer-to-peer architecture.
Shared backbone with appropriate termination at ends.
Individual endpoint links; central device dependency.
Closed loop; token passing is one historical access method.
Four nodes, six links; n(n-1)/2 unique connections.
Selected redundant links balance cost and resilience.
Hierarchical network; upstream failures affect branches.
Mesh backbone with star-based access LANs.
Active forwarding nodes depend on intermediate links.
C failure separates A/B from D/E; D/E may still communicate.
One redundant path non-forwarding prevents a Layer 2 loop.
Typical high-speed CAN: 120 ohm termination at each end.
Separate access branches; database reachable via backend.
